title: Importing, exporting, and backing up data

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Importing, exporting, and backing up data”?
options: The SQLite commands import CSV and export query results; other DBMSs use their own tools.
Start with a small, readable SELECT query; connect it to an application only after you understand its result.
SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
The query returns Ada and 42 in two columns.
questions.answer: The SQLite commands import CSV and export query results; other DBMSs use their own tools.
questions.explanation:
The SQLite commands import CSV and export query results; other DBMSs use their own tools.
Why: Loading a table from CSV and exporting results are common for analysis and moving data between systems. In the SQLite shell, `.mode csv` and `.import students.csv students` import a CSV; `.headers on`, `.once result.csv`, and a SELECT can write results to CSV. PostgreSQL's psql `\copy` works with a file on the client machine; MySQL `LOAD DATA` may require server permissions. Check the schema and encoding first, and never concatenate untrusted CSV values into SQL text. Backup tools include SQLite `.backup`, PostgreSQL `pg_dump`, and MySQL `mysqldump`; store backups separately and test restores.
